requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
The requirement is met. Every obligation has code that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Where the logic lives.** The run-forming and ownership logic is in `src/outline/mod.rs`: `assign_comments`, `trails_code`, `trailing_owner` and `run_owner`. None of these has its own `{impl}` reference. They are reachable from marked items:
- `reference_selector` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`, `citation_items` in `src/citations.rs` and `reference_set_entries` in `src/evidence.rs` all call `outlines.parse` and `owner_at_line`.
- `unreferenced_items` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` calls `outline::parse_with`.
- `parse` and `parse_with` reach `assign_comments` through the builder's `finish`.

So no reference gap arises.

**Obligations and code**
- **Consecutive comments form one run.** `assign_comments` joins a comment to the previous one when three things hold. Both have the same `binds_to_container` value, neither trails code, and the gap between them is blank. The comment must also start on the line right after the previous one ends, so a blank line splits runs.
- **A comment after other source on its line forms a run by itself.** `trails_code` is true when anything, including another comment, precedes the comment on its line. Such a comment never joins a run, and `trailing_owner` gives it the innermost node covering that line, which is the root if no node does.
- **Any other run belongs to the next node starting after it within the smallest containing node.** `run_owner` finds the smallest containing node and then its next child starting at or after the run's end.
- **A run with no following node belongs to its container.** `run_owner` falls back to the container, which is the root at top level.
- **A profile may bind a comment kind to its container.** The `comment_binds_to_container` field of `Profile` does this. `run_owner` returns the container when the flag is set.
- **The Rust profile binds inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container.** `PROFILE` in `src/outline/rust.rs` sets `comment_binds_to_container: is_inner_doc_comment`, so a file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root.
- **Markdown comments are HTML comment blocks.** `is_comment` in `src/outline/markdown.rs` accepts only `html_block` nodes that start with `<!--` and end with `-->`, so an inline HTML comment stays paragraph text of its section.
- **A reference in a comment counts for the node its run belongs to.** `owner_at_line` returns the comment's owner first. `reference_selector` uses it for authoring inputs, and `unreferenced_items` uses each comment's `owner` for Rust item coverage.

**Tests.** The `{test}` references in `src/outline/tests.rs` cover each case:
- `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next` covers consecutive lines forming one run.
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` and `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` cover next-node ownership, trailing comments, and the container fallback.
- `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` cover the container and root fallbacks.
- `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers a comment after another comment.
- `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` and the `//!` case in `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` cover inner doc binding.
- `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers all supported languages.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers Markdown.
- The YAML tests cover the YAML profile's trailing-comment handling.
- `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run` in `src/fenced.rs` shows a blank line separating runs.
- `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` covers the authoring-input contribution.
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` covers Rust item coverage.

I found no unspecified behavior and no gaps.

Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.

An in-source `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference to the subject, except a `{fixme}` inside one of the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, contributes the source containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
